findings.title: The `codex` extra is being introduced twice with conflicting content
findings.description: D1 declares `codex = ["openai-codex>=0.159.3,<1"]` and says it "Replaces the stale pyproject comment about GitHub installs." But slice 907 (Optional Dependency Split, status `deferred`) already owns the `[codex]` extra: its task T2.4 adds `codex = []` (PyPI rejects direct URL references, so it is an *empty* placeholder with a comment carrying the manual GitHub install command), and its success criteria assert that empty entry. Today's `pyproject.toml` still carries 907's comment block, and 907 remains deferred rather than superseded. When 129 lands, the `codex` extra exists in the tree twice — 907's placeholder plus 129's populated list — with no note in either direction recording the conflict. The requirement left unmet: a single source of truth for the extra's definition, and a coherent deferral record for 907. The design should either record that 907 is superseded (or that 129's extra fulfills its `codex` half) or defer the pyproject change until 907's status is settled.

findings.title: The OPENAI_API_KEY fallback verification exceeds the scope the slice plan assigned to this slice
findings.description: The slice plan entry (129, part C) assigns: interactive login, device-code, `auth.json` as the only store, `sq auth status` showing email/plan, and `sq auth logout`. It says nothing about the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback in `OAuthFileStrategy`. The design, however, adds a first implementation task — Development Approach step 0, "Verify the `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback against the real runtime … before porting anything" — with a two-branch outcome (keep-and-label the fallback, or remove it from `is_valid`/`active_source`/`get_credentials`/`setup_hint`), gated on a live probe with a real ChatGPT account. That is scope beyond the plan entry: a behavioral change to credential resolution for API-key users (currently `is_valid()` returns True for a key-only environment — verified in `src/squadron/providers/codex/auth.py`) plus a prerequisite external dependency the plan does not name. The rationale is legitimate (it prevents a silent-fallback false "authenticated"), but per the slice-plan alignment criteria, scope the plan entry did not assign should be either (a) added to the plan entry, or (b) named as cuttable/deferrable so a PM decision records the expansion. As written, the design silently widens the slice.

findings.title: `codex.turn_timeout_s` default (1800 s) is designed in, but the version pin is deferred to the PM
findings.description: D7 registers `codex.turn_timeout_s` with a concrete default of 1800 s "beside `cf.mcp_timeout_s`" (the existing precedent, verified in `config/keys.py`), which correctly centralizes the default at the config layer. In the same D1, the dependency spec ships with `openai-codex>=0.159.3,<1` while the upper bound is explicitly "not decided here … PM to say whether to cap." The asymmetry is defensible — a cap on a moving 0.x surface is a risk posture, 1800 s is an engineering choice with stated rationale — but it means implementation can begin with a dependency range whose final form is not the design's. No action required beyond the PM decision the design already names.

findings.title: `sq auth status` row enrichment is async, but the current command is a synchronous typer function
findings.description: The "Status" data flow appends account email/plan via `account()`, which runs `AsyncCodex` (runtime start + RPC, bounded by `codex.account_timeout_s`) — an async I/O path with its own enumerated failure row. The shipped `auth_status()` in `src/squadron/cli/commands/auth.py` is a synchronous function (strategies' `is_valid()`/`active_source` are sync). The design does not state how the async call is driven (e.g., `asyncio.run` in the command vs. an async command), and the "byte-for-byte unchanged" criterion for other profiles constrains the refactor. Small mechanism, but it is the one place the design's own failure-mode machinery (account timeout/cancel) has to be reached from the CLI layer, so it should be one sentence in the API Contracts section.

findings.title: Auth capability is additive and consistent with the architecture's Authentication Patterns
findings.description: The 100 HLD requires each provider's credential resolution to be self-contained and explicitly says squadron "does not attempt to unify authentication." The design's `InteractiveLogin` is an optional, `runtime_checkable` capability protocol that only `OAuthFileStrategy` implements, delegates entirely to the Codex runtime, stores no squadron-side credentials (`~/.codex/auth.json` stays the only store), and is dispatched via `isinstance` rather than the profile-name/auth-type string checks slice 128 banned (verified: 128's technical requirements and the shipped `AUTH_STRATEGIES` registry match the design's prerequisites). The design also correctly scopes the `AuthStrategy` Protocol itself as unchanged (D3's ISP rationale), and the dependency direction is right: CLI (interface layer) → auth capability (provider layer), which is the same direction as today's `auth_login`/`auth_status` consuming `resolve_auth_strategy_for_profile`.

findings.title: Failure modes and the runtime-startup NFR are explicit for every new I/O path
findings.description: Every new I/O path has enumerated failure rows with concrete handling: turn hang (`asyncio.timeout(codex.turn_timeout_s)`, cancel + `ProviderError`), mid-turn transport close (`TransportClosedError` → `ProviderError`, agent state reset so the dead client is not reused), server busy / rate-limit, token rejection, failed/interrupted status, empty `final_response` (D8 removes the current `result.final_response or ""` — verified present in `src/squadron/providers/codex/agent.py`), and teardown. Login `wait()` has its own timeout with `handle.cancel()` on timeout/Ctrl-C, and `account()` failure in `sq auth status` degrades to validity-without-account without failing the command. The slice touches a path with a stated NFR (100 HLD: SDK client subprocess startup cost, "design for warm pool / instance reuse rather than per-message creation"; 931: reviews measured at 1273 s wall-clock), and the design restates it with a specific treatment — spawn once per `CodexAgent` and never per message, spawning confined to three named call sites, startup duration at DEBUG, and an explicit "no latency target" rationale instead of a TBD. A per-row test requirement pins each signal. No silent fallbacks; `usage` absent stays `None`, never 0.

findings.title: Integration points match what the consuming/providing slices ship
findings.description: Verified against the shipped code and the two dependency designs: `ProviderCapabilities.applies_effort` exists (`src/squadron/providers/base.py:59`), the OpenAI agent already stamps `metadata["usage"]`/`["turns"]` via `_stamp_tool_telemetry` (so D6's "same metadata keys" reuse needs no review-artifact change), `ensure_provider_loaded`/`get_provider` are the real loader/registry entry points D9 routes `sq model list` through, `resolve_codex_binary()` and its callers are the exact surface D2 replaces, `cf.mcp_timeout_s` is the config-layer precedent D7 follows, and the doctor's existing `codex CLI` row (which gates the agents skills row) is correctly left untouched. Exclusions are appropriately drawn (streaming/tool plumbing out, `login_api_key` out, no squadron token store), and the slice delivers exactly what the plan entry's parts A/B/C assign.
